extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF text and Fig. 1-6 locators; unsupported scaffold claims about inflammation, membrane disruption, or nucleic-acid interaction were not promoted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Piscidin-1, caerin, and maculatin are supported as directly virucidal against PRV in source-reviewed TCID50 and plaque-reduction assays where virus was pre-incubated with peptide before cell exposure.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The direct mechanism is bounded to virion inactivation/direct interaction in the assay design; molecular target, membrane disruption, or nucleic-acid binding is not directly demonstrated for PRV in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The absence of detectable pre-infection or post-infection protection supports the authors' interpretation that these peptides primarily act by direct interaction with PRV particles under the tested conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a stage-of-infection inference, not a direct molecular binding or structural assay.

source_locator.label: Results: pre/post/direct infection-stage assay

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptide treatment of PRV before infection reduced downstream PRV-induced apoptosis in PK-15 cells, supporting a cell-protection outcome downstream of virucidal activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Peptide-treated PRV infection of PK-15 cells
mechanism_claims.limitations: Annexin V/PI apoptosis reduction is not itself a primary antimicrobial mechanism and is interpreted downstream of reduced infectious virus.

source_locator.label: Results: apoptosis assay

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Piscidin-1 co-injection reduced first-challenge PRV mortality in BALB/c mice, supporting in vivo antiviral efficacy but not a separate molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Piscidin-1 in BALB/c PRV-Ea challenge model
mechanism_claims.limitations: Protection was not durable after PRV rechallenge; this is retained as efficacy evidence, not mechanism-of-action proof.

rejected_or_bounded_claims.resolution: Discussion speculation is preserved as context only; final direct_mechanism remains virion inactivation/direct interaction by assay design.
No paper-local source evidence supports a nucleic-acid interaction mechanism for these peptide/virus assays.
